question:
A 46-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. He has type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. Current medications include metformin and lisinopril. He reports that he has adhered to his diet and medication regimen. His hemoglobin A1c is 8.6%. Insulin glargine is added to his medication regimen. Which of the following sets of changes is most likely to occur in response to this new medication?
$$$ Glycolysis %%% Glycogenesis %%% Lipolysis %%% Gluconeogenesis $$$?
analysis: Insulin glargine, a long-acting insulin, primarily works by promoting glucose uptake by tissues and by inhibiting hepatic glucose production. This results in increased glycogenesis (storage of glucose as glycogen) and decreased gluconeogenesis (production of new glucose). Additionally, insulin inhibits lipolysis (breakdown of fats) and has no direct effect on glycolysis (breakdown of glucose for energy), which is primarily regulated by cellular energy needs. Therefore, the addition of insulin glargine is likely to lead to an increase in glycogenesis, a decrease in gluconeogenesis, and a decrease in lipolysis.
